facts.text: I am Nikki.
I am working on a project to understand how people think about purchasing board games and how they go about purchasing them.
I am a user experience researcher at a company.
I wanted to understand someone’s thoughts and thought process on how they go about purchasing board games.
I like board games.
I bought a board game called Charter Stone.
I saw Charter Stone in a board game store after having brunch with a friend.
I dropped into the board game store because it was near where I live.
I bought a few games at my local board game store before.
My local board game store is friendly and has a huge selection.
I went into the local board game store on Saturday to indulge in my hobbies.
I was walking past the board game store on the way back from brunch.
I was attracted to the Charter Stone box because it was a well-designed, clean, very white box.
The Charter Stone box had almost nothing on the front.
The Charter Stone box had a brief summary of the mechanics on the back.
I like legacy games.
I like village building games.
I use BoardGameGeek when buying board games.
I use BoardGameGeek to read forums, reviews, and ratings for board games.
I use BoardGameGeek reviews that take complexity, number of players, and mechanics into account.
I bought Charter Stone on the spot as an impulse buy.
I bought Charter Stone because I liked the theme and the artwork.
I looked up Charter Stone on BoardGameGeek while I was in the store.
I browsed on my phone in the store to see what BoardGameGeek and big reviewers said.
I picked up Charter Stone and wandered around the store to consider what else to buy.
I sometimes purchase board games without going to BoardGameGeek if I have played the game before.
My current favorite board game is the Game of Thrones board game.
I bought the Game of Thrones board game on Amazon.
I was introduced to the Game of Thrones board game by a friend who spent the day playing it with me.
I buy the Game of Thrones board game because I played it and had the experience.
I use BoardGameGeek as a proxy for other people’s experiences to decide whether a game would apply to me.
I trust the community of gamers about what games I will like.
I use BoardGameGeek when a game is new for me.
I use BoardGameGeek to validate information about how a game works.
I sometimes check BoardGameGeek when I am at home browsing online for a board game.
I use five or six big reviewers in addition to BoardGameGeek.
If I am not sure about a rule or if two rules seem conflicting, I go to BoardGameGeek before the official website.
I believe BoardGameGeek is an authoritative source for board games online.
I believe official companies can test games many times and that official answers get consolidated on BoardGameGeek.
I check BoardGameGeek even if a friend recommends a game, unless I have played it myself.
I get games recommended to me by friends.
I have many friends who play board games.
My friends have different preferences for board games.
Some of my friends enjoy almost the same games as I do.
If a friend recommends a game that matches my friends’ preferences, I would take it as a smart purchase right away.

events.text: I bought Charter Stone after brunch with a friend and while walking past a board game store.
I visited my local board game store because it is near where I live and it is close to where I was eating after brunch.
I went into the local board game store on Saturday to indulge in my hobbies.
I bought the Game of Thrones board game on Amazon after being introduced to it by a friend and spending the day playing it.
